title: When the Summit Breaks
premise: Mara Yarrow, a railroad engineer drifting between closed mountain lines to stay off the books, is handed a dying prospector's map of the Kestrel River's forbidden headwaters in exchange for a promise: deliver it to his estranged daughter before the mining concession permits expire and the valley is sealed forever. Pursued by a concession company that wants the map buried with its secrets, Mara joins forces with the prospector's daughter, a disgraced surveyor named Ilsa, and follows the river upstream through collapsing tunnels, flooded camps, and a town that remembers too much. At the source they find not treasure but evidence of a covered-up disaster that explains both men's guilt—and Mara must choose between selling the proof for a new identity or publishing it and losing everything. They publish it, trading invisibility for a place in the found family they built on the river.
about_author: Ansel Oyelaran is a former track inspector who spent a decade walking abandoned rail lines across three continents before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and protagonists who measure trust in miles.

chapters.title: The Last Scheduled Train
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Riding a decommissioned line as a paid 'inspector' who inspects nothing, Mara establishes their rules of survival: never stay past the permit date, never use your real name. When the line's final crew abandons them mid-route, the beat is loneliness disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a rust-belt saloon, dying prospector Ede Voss trades Mara a hand-drawn map of the Kestrel headwaters for one promise: take it to his daughter before the concessions expire in six weeks. Mara accepts to be polite to a dead man—then finds a concession enforcer searching Voss's room. Beat: guilt arrives uninvited.

chapters.title: Ilsa of the Flooded Camp
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Mara tracks Voss's daughter to a drowned mining camp where Ilsa Voss, stripped of her surveyor's license, maps floodwaters no one will pay for. She refuses the map, then recognizes her father's handwriting and the lie that ruined him. Beat: grief hardening into purpose; uneasy alliance formed.

chapters.title: Permit Expiry
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The concession company voids all access permits early, sealing the valley legally while sending 'security contractors' after the map physically. Mara and Ilsa slip upstream ahead of the closure through a tunnel only Mara's rail knowledge can navigate. Beat: the chase begins; trust tested under pressure.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A rope-ferry crossing goes wrong; Ilsa saves Mara at the cost of the supply raft, and they shelter in an abandoned workers' barracks where Ilsa reveals her father mapped the river the year of the collapse he was blamed for. Beat: found family takes root around a shared fire.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The pair detour through Halloway, a company town where survivors of the old disaster recognize Voss's map and quietly feed them, hide them, and warn that the contractors have a photograph of Mara. An old woman gives Ilsa her father's letters. Beat: the past becomes an ally.

chapters.title: Switchback
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ambushed on a cliffside switchback, Mara bargains with contractor leader Renn using forged permit numbers, buying two days—but betrays nothing about Ilsa. Renn, himself once a rail man, lets them go with a warning that costs him. Beat: Mara discovers they can't stay invisible and keep their promises.

chapters.title: Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Starving and storm-bound above the treeline, the two nearly turn back; a near-fatal fall forces each to admit why they can't stop—Mara's buried culpability in a bridge failure, Ilsa's need to clear her father. Beat: confession as survival; the climb resumes lighter.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the headwaters they find the sealed adit Voss mapped: inside, survey records proving the company dynamited its own dam and blamed the workers—including Voss. Contractors arrive; Renn, seeing the documents, stands down his team. Beat: climax—the truth is worth more than the silence it bought.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Rather than vanish with the records, Mara and Ilsa release them through Halloway's survivors and the last open rail line, ending the concessions and Voss's disgrace. Mara uses their real name for the first time in years. Beat: resolution—staying visible, staying put, together.
